newsitem.title: norway: SOCCER-LIVERPOOL EYE SEMIS AFTER ESCAPING WITH A DRAW.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-LIVERPOOL EYE SEMIS AFTER ESCAPING WITH A DRAW.

text.p: Brann Bergen's
part-timers held the expensive taltents of Liverpool to a 1-1
draw in the first leg of their European Cup Winners' Cup
quarter-final on Thursday and almost pulled off a shock victory.
But Brann's failure to win at home has tipped the tie
Liverpool's way, although after losing at home after drawing
away in the UEFA Cup to Brondby of Denmark last season,
Liverpool will not underestimate their Scandinavian opponents in
the return leg in two weeks time.
Only two stunning saves by Liverpool goalkeeper David James
in the dying minutes spared Liverpool's blushes on a night when
manager Roy Evans will not have been happy with his team's
performance.
Liverpool started dramatically with England striker Robbie
Fowler finally finding the net in audacious style after wasting
a hatful of chances in his last two games.
Fowler ran on to a 40 metre pass from defender Neil Ruddock
before back- heeling the ball over the head of defender Per Ove
Ludvigsen and ferociously volleying the ball home with his left
foot to give Liverpool a ninth minute lead. It was his fourth
fourth goal in the tournament this season and his fourth from
his first seven games.
Playing in front of a 12,000 strong crowd with thousands of
Liverpool's Norwegian fans cheering the away team, Liverpool
spent the rest of the first half playing an edgy possesion game.
But the Norwegians clawed their way back into the match,
mainly thanks to the persistence of striker Tore Andre Flo, who
is reported to be set to be the latest in a long line of
Norwegians to join an English club. Ironically, the rumours are
that Liverpool are prepared to pay 4.0 million pounds for him.
At halftime, Mons Ivar Mjelde - the top Norwegian goalscorer
- who had been suffering from infuelnza - was brought on an made
an instant impression.
He fired just wide of the Liverpool goal and then after 476
minutes, with Brann players pouring forward striker Geir Hasund
reacted to the ball quicker than the Liverpool defenders around
him and swept the ball home off the left-hand post okeeper
David James.
Liverpool, sorely missing the defensive stability of
injured Mark Wright, were stunned back into action and Fowler
hit the bar with an exquisitely flighted lob over goalkeeper
Vidar Bahus.
But the Norwegians were not overawed and fought back again,
Flo firing the ball twice in the dying minutes only to see James
make desparate saves.
Liverpool hung on for the draw and will now look forward to
the return leg at Anfield in two weeks time with cautious
optimism.
Liverpool manager Roy Evans was a relieved man afterwards
telling the assembled media: "As we predicted, it was a tough
game. They said they would make it difficult for us and they did
just that.
"We cooled after a good opening, but overall I was happy
with the result. It was a truly great goal by Robbie Fowler.
It's nice to see one go in for a change.
"It's nice to have the away goal, but it's not over yet.
They are one tough team and their record speaks for itself."
Liverpool, who have won both the European Cup and UEFA
Cup, are bidding to win the Cup Winners Cup for the first time
to join the select band of clubs consisting only of Barcelona,
Bayern Munich, Ajax and Juventus, who have won all three
European club trophies.
